literal: Eyes also taking along you go, O heart! These me will eat, him seeing desiring.
translation: O heart, take my eyes along with you when you go; otherwise, in their intense desire to see him, they will eat me alive.
modern: நெஞ்சே! நீ அவரிடம் செல்லும்போது என் கண்களையும் உடன் கூட்டிக்கொண்டு போ; இல்லையென்றால், அவரைப் பார்க்க வேண்டும் என்று விரும்பி, இந்தக் கண்கள் என்னை அரித்துத் தின்றுவிடும்.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine addresses her own heart which is rushing to be with her beloved. She begs her heart to take her eyes along on its journey. She fears that if the eyes are left behind, their desperate longing to see him will torment and consume her. The metaphor of the eyes 'eating' her vividly portrays the painful, gnawing sensation of unfulfilled desire.
